name: ZeroQuant: Efficient and Affordable Post-Training Quantization for Large-Scale Transformers
authors: Lin, Yang, Tang, Zheng, Li, Chen, Dai
problem: Quantization overhead (quantize/dequantize kernels) and calibration data cost made quantization of large models uneconomic in practice.
mechanism: Three-component pipeline: (1) fine-grained hardware-friendly group-wise quantization with per-group scales and asymmetric quantization to halve scale overhead; (2) layer-by-layer knowledge distillation (LKD) that needs no original training data - the teacher is the unquantized layer and the calibration inputs are synthetic activations propagated forward from layer 0; (3) a custom quantization system backend that fuses quant/dequant into the matmul to remove the runtime overhead.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): INT8 weights+activations at 'cost-free' accuracy impact with up to 5.19x (BERT) and 4.16x (GPT-3 style) speedup vs FP16 inference; adding LKD gives INT4 fully-connected + INT8 attention with 3x memory-footprint reduction vs FP16. COMPRESSION RATIO: 8x for the W8A8 config, ~4x for the mixed INT4/INT8 config. QUALITY COST: described as 'minimal accuracy impact' - not quantified in the abstract. Hardware in the paper is the authors' own custom INT8 kernels, which is precisely why this did not become a production default: no general-purpose kernel ships it.
